segments.name: Cloud
segments.note: Cloud infrastructure (OCI) of $7.4B, up 121%, plus cloud applications (SaaS) of $4.2B, up 10% — now 60% of all revenue.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Traditional on-premise software licenses and support — shrinking as customers migrate to Oracle's cloud.

segments.name: Hardware
segments.note: Servers and engineered systems — a small but growing slice as AI data centers need machines.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building cloud and AI products — actually down 4% YoY as revenue surged.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud — down 12% YoY, leaner even as sales boom.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — flat vs a year ago.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — down from $420M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: One-off reorganization costs — down sharply from $415M a year ago.

oneTimers: Oracle sold $20B of new common stock in the quarter through an at-the-market program to fund its data-center expansion — helpful for the balance sheet, dilutive for existing shareholders.
verdict: Oracle's revenue jumped 30% to a record $19.3B as its cloud infrastructure business more than doubled — and customers have now signed $664B of future contracts, though building the data centers pushed free cash flow to −$5B.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $1,428M on Oracle's growing debt pile, partly offset by $307M of non-operating income.
footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud and software', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue. Net income of $4,760M is before $81M of preferred stock dividends; the $1.56 EPS uses the $4,679M available to common shareholders.

takeaways.title: The cloud build-out is the story
takeaways.text: Cloud infrastructure revenue more than doubled to $7.4B, and Oracle delivered 850MW of new data-center capacity and over 300,000 GPUs to AI customers in one quarter.

takeaways.title: A backlog bigger than most companies
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — contracts customers have signed but not yet paid for — hit $664B, up $209B in a year, including $30B+ of new AI cloud contracts in this quarter alone.

takeaways.title: Record cash in, even more spent
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow hit a record $23B, yet free cash flow was −$5B because data-center construction is consuming cash even faster. Oracle also sold $20B of new stock to help fund it.

follow100Note: Kept-as-profit includes −$5.79 of other expense per $100 of revenue; the rows add to $99.99 due to rounding.
